key_impacts: PHIVOLCS issued tsunami alert level 3 (immediate evacuation) for coastal areas of Northern Samar, Eastern Samar, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur after the 31 August 2012 earthquake.
No significant tsunami was observed and no damages were reported; PHIVOLCS canceled the alert at 12:10 am on 1 September 2012.

In parts of Eastern Samar (e.g., Guiuan), the warning reached people after the expected wave arrival; travel time to Guiuan was ~10 minutes while the PHIVOLCS warning was released 14 minutes after the quake.
Communication problems were reported: non-working or absent mobile signals, major power cuts, and incorrect radio information in one municipality, causing delayed/distorted messages.
Surveyed barangays reported an estimated average of about 80% of residents evacuating; some self-evacuated after feeling the earthquake and officials generally guided evacuations.
missing_information: Exact number of evacuees by location.

events.event_hazard: Distant-source tsunami alert (triggered by the 27 Feb 2010 Chile earthquake)
key_impacts: A tsunami alert was raised in the Philippines at the end of February 2010 following the distant 27 February 2010 Chile earthquake.
Only a very small wave occurred and no damages were reported in the Philippines.
Because the source was distant, time was not an important factor in the related survey of warnings/evacuations.
missing_information: Specific Philippine regions/provinces covered by the alert.
Number of evacuees and locations of evacuations.
Arrival times and any measured wave heights at Philippine coasts.
Details on communication performance and dissemination chain during the 2010 alert.
